    Connect to your tenant

    One read-only sign-in covers all three views. Register a single-page application with delegated, read-only Microsoft Graph permissions; the User, Workload and Agent views each read what they need from the one token. Global Reader is enough; nothing here writes to the tenant.

    Create it with a script

    PowerShell 7 + the Microsoft.Graph module (Install-Module Microsoft.Graph), signed in as a Global Administrator. It creates the SPA app, adds this page's redirect URI, requests every permission below and grants admin consent, then prints the Client ID and Tenant ID. Scope IDs resolve by name at runtime, so it never goes stale.

    
          
    Re-running updates the same app and keeps redirect URIs already registered. Another host? Pass -RedirectUri "https://yourhost/Entra-Posture.html". Prefer clicking through the portal? Use Manual (portal).

        Attack path — the highest-risk combination, read left to right as one AND
        
          ?Why this compound: privilege is only as strong as the credential in front of it, and only as contained as the gate in front of that. A permanent write role means there is no activation step to notice or approve; Tier-0 means the role is GA-class; weak or no MFA means the credential is phishable. Together that is one phish away from the top of the directory.

    How to read it: left to right as one AND. The big number is how many accounts carry that factor and every factor before it, so it can only fall; the small number is how many carry that factor anywhere in the tenant. Colour is the severity the chain has reached; a green zero means the AND leaves nobody behind. Disabled accounts are excluded — they cannot sign in. Click a card to scope the table.

        Attack path — the highest-risk combination, read left to right as one AND
        
          ?Why this compound: a multi-tenant app registered in another tenant, holding application permissions, is app-only access with no signed-in user, no Conditional Access and no session to expire — on a credential that lives in the publisher’s tenant and that you cannot rotate. A high-privilege scope and an unverified publisher are the escalators on top of that.

    How to read it: left to right as one AND. The big number is how many apps carry that factor and every factor before it, so it can only fall; the small number is how many hold that factor anywhere in the tenant. Colour is the severity the chain has reached; a green zero means the AND leaves nobody behind. Disabled service principals are excluded — they cannot authenticate, so their key is dormant. Click a card to scope the table to its cohort.

        Query engine
        Ask the graph
        
        
        Ask in plain English. The question is translated into a graph query — the translated query is shown and stays editable, so every answer is a real query over the collected graph, never a guess. With a local AI model configured it understands free-form questions; without one it falls back to built-in phrasings.
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        Advanced grammar
          
        
            
        paths from <selector> to <selector> [via <edge|type>] [all] [limit N] · nodes <selector> · who can reach <selector> · what can <selector> reach · edges <EdgeKind>
        
            
        Selectors combine freely: type:user|guest|group|role|app|sp|mi|agent|blueprint|device|permission|issuer|partner|tenant name:"text" role:"Global Administrator" perm:"Directory.ReadWrite.All" critical privileged guest disabled synced nomfa dormant caexcluded secret cert fic eligible permanent owner id:<guid>
        
            
        Edge kinds: 
        
          
        
        
        
        
        
      
        
    
        

    
    
        
      
        
        
        
          
        Collector
        Sources, permissions, audit
        
          
        Every Graph call is read-only, rate-limit aware (429 → Retry-After), tenant-scoped and logged. The matrix shows which permission each source needs and whether the connected identity had it.
        
          
        
          
        
          
        
        
        
        
        
          
        Export
        Take it with you
        
          
        Findings, attack paths, inventories, graph relationships, critical assets and remediation — as JSON, CSV or a self-contained HTML report (print it for PDF).
        
          
        
          
        Critical assets
        
          
        Tier-0 roles, role-assignable groups, service principals with tier-0 Graph permissions and the tenant are marked automatically. Right-click any node in the graph, or use the ★ in a detail panel, to add custom ones. Stored per tenant in this browser.
